item.text:
**8B.7 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**
Net assessment: mostly no. Some targeted service-delivery and reform indicators moved in the claimed direction, but the dominant 2024 outcome picture was macro stress, rising poverty/inequality risk, major schooling disruption, and a severe lethal crackdown.

**Partial positives**
- [IMF Executive Board Concludes the Second Review under the ECF/EFF/RSF for Bangladesh](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/24/pr24234-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2nd-review-ecf-eff-rsf) | IMF | June 24, 2024 | The IMF said Bangladesh had already taken corrective macro steps, including exchange-rate realignment, tighter monetary policy, and tax/subsidy reforms; it also projected FY24 growth at 5.4% and inflation easing later, so the direction was partially consistent with stabilization claims, but still conditional and not yet a broad outcome success. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`

- [WHO Bangladesh Celebrates Landmark Success of the Health and Gender Support Project in Cox’s Bazar](https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/22-06-2024-who-bangladesh-celebrates-landmark-success-of-the-health-and-gender-support-project-in-cox-s-bazar) | WHO Bangladesh | June 22, 2024 | This is one of the clearest 2024 positive outcome items: the project reported 544,000+ people screened, nearly 1,000 health workers trained, and expanded NCD/TB/lab/EWARS capacity in a vulnerable area. That is real service-delivery gain, though narrow and partner-financed. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`

- [World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co) | World Bank | May 28, 2024 | World Bank-backed projects funded health, nutrition, education, water, shelters, livelihoods, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities. This points to some measurable welfare gains for vulnerable groups, but the effect is targeted and externally financed rather than broad national improvement. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`

- [Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r) | World Bank | April 2, 2024 | The World Bank described Bangladesh as having a strong post-COVID turnaround, so there was still some positive momentum in the economy. But the report is only a partial positive because it immediately notes that inflation, reserve pressure, and financial vulnerabilities were still distorting the path. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.3`

**Negative or off-target outcomes**
- [Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r) | World Bank | April 2, 2024 | The same World Bank update says the recovery was being disrupted by high inflation, a persistent balance-of-payments deficit, financial-sector vulnerabilities, and reserve pressure. That is direct evidence that a core claimed outcome, macro stability and purchasing power, was moving the wrong way in 2024. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`

- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672) | World Bank | October 1, 2024 | The Bank projected growth slowing to 4.0% in FY25, extreme poverty rising to 6.1% in FY24, and inequality increasing by more than one Gini point, with jobs and revenue mobilization still unresolved. That is strong negative evidence on the ruler’s claimed prosperity and inclusion outcomes. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.1`, `8B.3`

- [Bangladesh | World Bank Data](https://data.worldbank.org/country/bangladesh?lang=en) | World Bank | 2024 values on data page | The data page shows GDP growth at 4.2% and inflation at 10.5% for 2024. Growth remained positive, but the inflation reading is the more important directional signal here: living-cost pressure was still very high, so the net welfare effect was poor. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.3`

- [Bangladesh | World Bank Data](https://data.worldbank.org/country/bangladesh?lang=en) | World Bank | 2024 values on data page | This same dataset shows that Bangladesh’s outcome picture remained mixed rather than strongly improving: output still expanded, but the economy was not translating that into broad-based relief for households. It is a useful aggregate check, but not proof of successful delivery on the ruler’s claims. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.3`

- [Bangladesh](https://www.unicef.org/reports/learning-interrupted-global-snapshot-2024) | UNICEF | January 2025 | UNICEF’s retrospective on 2024 says climate hazards disrupted schooling for 35 million children in Bangladesh, with prolonged closures and large learning losses. That is strong negative evidence against progress on education/human capital outcomes, even allowing for climate constraints. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`

- [Bangladesh | UN OHCHR](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) | UN OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | The UN said more than 170 people had been killed, some injured people were denied medical care, and internet shutdowns increased impunity. This is strong evidence that resident safety and institutional legitimacy moved sharply in the wrong direction during the year’s central crisis. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`

- [Bangladesh Back UN Investigation Into Grave Abuses](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/26/bangladesh-back-un-investigation-grave-abuses) | Human Rights Watch | August 26, 2024 | HRW said the July crackdown was the deadliest in Bangladesh’s recent history, with at least 440 killed and extensive violence by law enforcement and Awami League-linked youth groups. This is very strong evidence that the 2024 outcome on civilian protection was substantially worse, not better. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`

- [Factbox: Troubled Bangladesh’s economy bogged down by high unemployment, inflation](https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1) | Reuters | August 8, 2024 | Reuters summarized widening current-account deficits, taka depreciation, falling reserves, IMF dependence, and stagnant private-sector job creation. That is a broad negative outcome signal on jobs, price stability, and macro resilience. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.3`, `8B.6`

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single official 2024 scoreboard that ties the Smart Bangladesh agenda to a clean national outcome dashboard across growth, poverty, jobs, education, and governance. The best evidence is therefore a patchwork of macro reports, sectoral delivery data, and retrospective crisis reporting, which makes the judgment directional rather than mechanically measurable.
